Q: Python algorithm to automatically propagate inequalities transitively A:

you might want to look into the graphlib module from the standard library. It implements a topological sorter, which is basically exactly what you want.

Q: SwiftUI add image to left side of text field A:

You can use this simple modifier:

.safeAreaInset(edge: .leading) { Image(systemName: "lock") }

💡 It works on any kind of View not just the TextField.

Demo Code of the above image:
TextField("Password", text: $password)
    .safeAreaInset(edge: .leading) { Image(systemName: "lock") }
    .padding(.all)
    .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 10))

💡 Pro Tip

Don't forget to add a simple tapGesture to the background to select the textField and enhance the selection experience.

Q: In diamond-pattern virtual inheritance, why does the most derived class look for the default constructor of the indirect virtual base? A:

virtual base classes are special in that they are initialized by the most derived class and not by any intermediate base classes that inherits from the virtual base. Which of the potential multiple initializers would the correct choice for initializing the one base?

If the most derived class being constructed does not list it in its member initalization list then the virtual base class is initialized with its default constructor which must exist and be accessible.

Note that a virtual base identifier is allowed to be use in a constructor's initializer list even if it is not a direct base of the class in question.

Q: How do I avoid left padding in menu items after upgrading from Java 21 to Java 25? A:

It was concluded that it was not a bug and is required behavior to fix another issue:

This change in UI is needed to fix rendering of radiobutton and/or checkmark as done in JDK-8348760.

It is also in sync with what windows does if menuitem selection is needed via radiobutton or checkmark as seen in attached screenshot icon-view.png

See JDK-8370945

However, a more recent comment suggests that it's being reconsidered :

The extra padding should not be needed unless there is actually a radio button anywhere. If there's none at all, the layout can be as it used to be.

For the time being, an alternative is to turn to other look and feels such as Flatlaf.

Q: How to scale text dynamically? A:

The Using Fonts Tutorial from the Godot documentation has a ton of detail about many different aspects of font rendering and I'd highly recommend giving it a read through.

Specifically regarding text scaling, the most relevant sections are:

  • Dynamic Fonts
  • MSDF Font Rendering

Incorporating these should give the desired result you're hoping for!
